whatTheseAre: Three consecutive records from a REAL working session's transcript, spanning one async
subagent launch: the assistant `tool_use` (name Agent), the `tool_result` that closes the
CALL but not the work (toolUseResult.isAsync true, status async_launched), and the later
user record whose string content is the <task-notification> that reports completion and
Captured because claude 2.1.276+ made Agent launches ASYNC, which silently broke Flight
Deck's sidebar subagent count: the count went +1 on the tool_use and -1 on the launch
result inside one poll, so it read 1 then 0 while the agent was still running.
editingRule: DELIBERATELY NOT VERBATIM, unlike dialogs.captured.provenance.json's batch, whose rule is
'lines may be DROPPED, never EDITED'. That rule fits a synthetic dialog capture; it does
not fit three records lifted out of a real working session, which carry absolute home
paths, a subagent prompt and an agent's full prose result. Kept in its own provenance file
rather than added to that batch, so the batch's verbatim guarantee stays true.
Edits applied, and nothing else: absolute /Users/... paths -> /REDACTED; the Agent
tool_use `input` -> {description, prompt} both 'REDACTED'; the tool_result content string
-> a fixed 'Async agent launched successfully.'; toolUseResult reduced to the marker keys
Every field the rows actually assert on is UNEDITED: the tool_use id and name, the

capturedBy: Lifted from ~/.claude/projects by scripts run in the session that added the rows, then
redacted as above. Chosen as the first launch in the file whose result AND notification
were both present, so the triple is genuinely consecutive rather than assembled.

everyAgentLaunchCarriesTheAsyncMarker: CONFIRMED and strong. Measured over 4 real transcripts spanning claude 2.1.278-2.1.283:
177 Agent launches, 177 tool_results with toolUseResult.isAsync true. No exceptions.
everyAgentLaunchIsEventuallyClosedByANot: FALSE -- do NOT pin this. 19 of those same 177 launches (10.7%) are never closed by a
task-notification carrying their id, and they are not merely in flight: in one 4680-line
transcript the 5 unclosed launches sit at 17%, 39%, 43%, 76% and 83% through the file,
while launches that DO close are closed 7-15 lines later. A consumer that decrements only
on a notification therefore LEAKS about one in ten launches.
The mirror also happens: 11 notification ids in that file have no launch in the file at
all (one transcript had 4 notification ids and zero launches), so a bare decrement can
fire for work never counted. Compaction is the obvious suspect; NOT established.

notCaptured: A SYNCHRONOUS Agent launch -- a tool_result for an Agent call WITHOUT isAsync. Every one of
the 177 launches measured was async, so the synchronous arm of the proposed invariant could
not be captured and is not asserted by any row.
A launch whose notification never arrives, and an orphan notification whose launch is
absent. Both are known to occur (see verdicts) but are a LIVENESS property over a whole
session, not a shape a three-record fixture can carry.
